text:
claire_cust: Hi team, urgent — Acme Corp couldn't pay invoice INV-1029 via the hosted invoice link. Their finance says the corporate virtual card returns a decline. No decline code on our UI, just "Payment failed". cc @anya_support

anya_support: Sorry to hear that — can you confirm last4 + card network? Also which link (hosted) and amount?

claire_cust: Last4 4242, Visa virtual, amount $12,345.67 USD. Client screenshot attached shows a generic error. They tried twice.

anya_support: Thanks. Pinging payments team. @payments-bot can you pull the gateway response for txn attempt with invoice_id=INV-1029 and last4=4242?

payments-bot: Found events for invoice=INV-1029, card_last4=4242: 2 auth_attempts. Gateway response snippets: `{"status":"declined","code":"card_declined","provider_code":"do_not_honor"}` then `{"status":"declined","code":"not_allowed","provider_detail":"card_not_allowed_for_merchant_category"}`.

leo_accounting: That second provider_detail looks like an MCC restriction — client vendor MCC might be flagged by the card issuer. Acme's card policy blocks some MCC categories for virtual cards by default.

claire_cust: Acme confirms they have a corporate spend policy blocking 'software' and 'miscellaneous' categories for virtuals. But this vendor is definitely 'B2B SaaS' which should be allowed.

sam_engineer: Sharing quick repro steps I ran on staging invoice flow: 1) create invoice with amount 123.45 2) call POST /payments/hosted_tokenize -> returned token 3) POST /payments/charge with token -> gateway responded with `not_allowed`. Sample gateway log: ```{"merchant_mcc":5734,"card_type":"VIRTUAL","issuer_response":"not_allowed","avs":"Y","cvv":"N","gateway":"stripe"}```

anya_support: Two possible vectors: issuer-level MCC policy on virtual cards OR our tokenization payload is missing merchant category so issuer flags it. Sam — can you confirm our token payload includes merchant_category?

sam_engineer: Yep we send merchant_category as 5734 in the token metadata. I compared a successful physical card run and virtual run — payloads match. Differences: virtual card BIN ranges get routed to a special processor and issuer enforces stricter rules (daily spend limit + MCC restrictions).

claire_cust: Client also reported a 3DS redirection briefly appeared then failed to complete — maybe issuer tried step-up auth then refused. Screenshot: "3DS challenge failed".

anya_support: Ok action items: 1) Ask client to try a non-virtual (physical) card as a quick workaround. 2) Ask acme finance to whitelist the vendor MCC for virtual cards or temporarily raise virtual card allowance. 3) We escalate to gateway / acquiring to see if we can get more granular decline code.

leo_accounting: Can we also create a manual one-off payment link (manual bank transfer / ACH) for this invoice while we sort card? Client prefers card but needs to avoid overdue.

claire_cust: They'll accept a wire if we provide details. Please generate temp invoice with wire instructions.

sam_engineer: I've opened ticket with our gateway (ticket GW-8821) and attached our logs + sample payloads. Requested explicit issuer decline reasons and whether 3DS step-up attempted.

payments-bot: GW-8821 created. Current status: awaiting gateway response (ETA 24-48h).

anya_support: In parallel, @claire_cust please ask Acme to call their card admin and request: "allow MCC 5734 for virtual cards" and check virtual card daily limit is >= $12,345.67. If they can try a physical corporate card that's faster.

claire_cust: On it. I'll update thread after they call. Thanks all :pray: 

(added later) claire_cust: Update — Acme called their card provider: issuer confirms virtual-card daily ceiling of $10k and MCC restrictions for software vendors. They temporarily raised the limit to $15k and removed the MCC block. They retried and payment succeeded.

anya_support: Great — closing as resolved. Note: we should add a KB entry for virtual-card limits + MCC failures on hosted invoice flow.

sam_engineer: Agree, I'll create a short doc under support KB with troubleshooting steps and gateway log examples.

claire_cust: Marking done. :white_check_mark:
